newsitem.title: JAPAN: Isuzu sees 97/98 parent oper prft Y32 bln.
newsitem.headline: Isuzu sees 97/98 parent oper prft Y32 bln.

text.p: Isuzu Motors Ltd said on Tuesday that it expects to post a parent operating profit of 32 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1998, down 3.3 percent compared with the previous fiscal year.
Isuzu managing director Hisayasu Yoshida told a news conference that the firm plans to increase its parent capital investment to 41 billion yen this fiscal year, up from 40.2 billion yen last year.
The higher capital investment would go to improving existing plants in Japan and to building new domestic facilities for engine production.
Yoshida said the firm expects its domestic vehicle sales to fall by 3.2 percent from last year to 153,000 units, and vehicle exports to rise by 8.9 percent from last year to 208,000 units.
Yoshida said Isuzu expects Japan's total domestic demand for heavy trucks to fall by 7,500 units this year to 145,000 units.
He said the firm expects its depreciation costs this year to fall to 33 billion yen from 34.9 billion last year.
He forecast that overseas production would fall by 0.6 percent to 361,000 units compared with last year.
